items.stem: A record stored in a blockchain block is altered after the block is chained. Why is this immediately detectable?

options.text: The block's hash changes, breaking the link every later block committed to
options.rationale: Correct: each block commits to the previous hash, so any edit cascades.

options.text: The network sends an email alert
options.rationale: There is no such mechanism; detection is cryptographic.

options.text: The ledger is encrypted so edits are impossible
options.rationale: Ledgers are tamper-evident, not encrypted against edits.

options.text: Only the miner can see the change
options.rationale: Any verifying node recomputes hashes and detects the mismatch.

items.explanation: Correct: each block commits to the previous hash, so any edit cascades.

items.stem: Which TWO properties genuinely require a decentralised blockchain rather than a well-run shared database? (Select TWO.)

options.text: No single party can be trusted to control the write history
options.rationale: Correct: removing a trusted central writer is a core blockchain use case.

options.text: Participants need verifiable, tamper-evident settlement without a central intermediary
options.rationale: Correct: trust-minimised settlement is a genuine blockchain property.

options.text: The team wants faster queries than a database
options.rationale: Databases are faster; speed is not a blockchain advantage.

options.text: The data must be stored only once to save disk
options.rationale: Blockchains replicate data across nodes, using more storage.

items.explanation: Correct: removing a trusted central writer is a core blockchain use case.

items.stem: A payment shows 1 confirmation on a public chain. Why might the merchant still wait before releasing goods?

options.text: A short chain reorganisation can orphan the block and revert the transaction
options.rationale: Correct: finality is probabilistic, so more confirmations reduce reorg risk.

options.text: The transaction fee has not been paid yet
options.rationale: An included transaction has already paid its fee.

options.text: One confirmation means the transaction failed
options.rationale: One confirmation means it was included once.

options.text: The merchant must manually approve each block

items.explanation: Correct: finality is probabilistic, so more confirmations reduce reorg risk.
